decisions.text: type line: a regular series whose pattern of change is the point (06 DP6-1, G1.51)
one shared scale: one scale for every panel, so that sizes compare across panels (G7.48)
the values are not far from zero compared with their spread
a legend instead of end labels: the label of Cash, Int'l would move 3.9 line heights from its line (at most 1.5 with a leader) (G5.3, G5.7)
no point markers: no value is isolated and no straight run hides one
the unit phrase on the top label: “$60K in donations”; the top gridline starts after it
digits hidden: thousands, stated once on the top label (R2-05, D-3): “$60K in donations”
time axis: row 2 (“2022”) left out, the title gives it (G2.37)

legend entries in the order of the lines at the latest point: Credit card, Central, Check, Central, Credit card, West, Check, West, Cash, Central, Credit card, North, Check, North, Cash, West, Check, East, Credit card, East, Cash, North, Cash, East, Credit card, Int'l, Check, Int'l, Cash, Int'l
the legend at the right of the plot, beside the latest values, centred on the plot

findings.message: panels.arrangement series in each panel by payment method and region departs from the procedure, which gives rows by payment method, columns by region (no comparison within a panel is stated (facts.compare): one series per panel, the most panels and the least clutter (13-15 DP-1))
findings.reason: the book's rejected version: every series in one chart
findings.recommended: rows by payment method, columns by region
findings.title: the arrangement of small multiples chosen for the insight, from the range of candidates

findings.message: 15 lines in one chart, crossing 32 times, not labelled directly: a general audience gets fewer series per panel, more panels (G1.20; five lines, D-28, a provisional threshold)
findings.title: no single chart of many overlapping series for a general audience

findings.message: 15 lines crossing 32 times, not labelled directly: more than five lines only if they rarely cross (about once per line) and are labelled directly; else small multiples (G1.20, D-28)
findings.title: at most about five lines, more only if they rarely cross and are labelled directly

findings.message: 15 regular colours: beyond eight they cannot be told apart; drop, group or merge categories, or label every series directly (G4.19, G4.21, D-14)
findings.reason: the book's rejected spaghetti chart (s. 0338), rebuilt: fifteen colours with a legend
findings.title: at most eight regular colours

findings.message: #94712a and #ba5c28 are 0.017 apart under deuteranopia (at least 0.06): readers with colour-vision deficiency may not tell them apart (G4.18, D-34)
findings.title: colours that must be told apart survive colour-vision deficiency

overrides.reason: the book's rejected spaghetti chart (s. 0338), rebuilt: fifteen colours with a legend

source.shows: the other end of the book's spectrum, rebuilt: all fifteen series in one chart, told apart only by a legend of fifteen colours; the generator warns that five lines in a plot are usually enough (G1.20) and lets the colours through only by an override

summary.arrangement: series in each panel by payment method and region
